question: Does the paper-defined x-prediction / v-loss parameterization improve late-time clean-expression behavior and generation at the same short budget?
paper_basis: OCOO-T v2 Eq.6, explicit parameterization ablation; primary Table3 default remains Eq.5 v-prediction. This unpatched diagnostic is not a claim of reproducing the patched Fig.5 experiments.
model_prediction_api: Forward always returns velocity. In x mode use (x_theta(z,t)-z)/(1-t). Existing velocity loss, EMA validation, literal CFG and Heun solver consume that velocity without a second conversion.

numerical_guard.reason: Finite denominator if a floating-point sampled time approaches 1. OCOO-T does not specify this guard; it is inactive on the Heun50 grid (largest model time 0.98).

initialization: Identical neural parameter initialization and RNG to shared v reference. The zero clean head has v=-z/(1-t), so initial functions and initial losses intentionally differ; do not require first-step loss equality.
primary_objective: PDCorr+mean(PDS_L1,PDS_L2,PDS_cos), raw and nonnegative reported separately; all nine nonnegative metrics and paired60-condition intervals.
additional_diagnostics: frozen buffers and initialized parameter compatibility

pre_launch_checks.result: 4 CPU tests passed1.60s: default exact legacy compatibility, untying compatibility, x/v weighted loss+gradient identity, zero x-head under actual Heun50

caveat: Short raw-weight pilot cannot establish mature EMA superiority or training-seed robustness. Main original v model continues unchanged; candidate must be labeled as an explicit parameterization ablation.
